response.summary: The user started Lantern, a home energy dashboard fed by an Octopus Home Mini, chose PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB over InfluxDB for storage and Grafana (suggested by Siyu) over a custom UI, and left downsampling as an open question.

facts.text: Lantern is a side project: a home energy dashboard.
Lantern reads an Octopus Home Mini smart meter every 30 seconds and shows usage, cost and a forecast for the day.
Readings must be stored for at least two years.
At 30-second resolution Lantern will store roughly 1 million readings a year.
Storage will be PostgreSQL with the TimescaleDB extension.
Lantern runs on a Raspberry Pi 4.
The dashboard will use Grafana rather than a custom UI for now.
Provides smart meter readings every 30 seconds through the Octopus API.
Octopus has changed the Home Mini API before.
The Home Mini provides 30-second data at no charge.
Chosen as Lantern's storage together with the TimescaleDB extension.
Easier to join readings against tariff tables than InfluxDB because it is relational.
Adds automatic time partitioning, continuous aggregates and compression to PostgreSQL.
Compression can shrink two years of readings to a few hundred megabytes.
Compression jobs can spike memory on a Raspberry Pi 4, so shared_buffers should be set conservatively.
Considered for Lantern storage: very fast ingest, but a second query language and a weaker story for joining with relational data.
Suggested by Siyu for the Lantern dashboard instead of a custom UI.
Talks to Postgres natively and provides time-range pickers, alerting and annotations.
A friend of the user from Shanghai, China.
A lawyer who tinkers with home automation at weekends.
Suggested Grafana for the Lantern dashboard.
Hosts Lantern; a 4 GB model runs Postgres fine.

decisions.question: Which storage should Lantern use for two years of 30-second meter readings?
decisions.reasoning: Familiar SQL, easy joins with tariff tables, automatic time partitioning, continuous aggregates and compression.
assumptions: The Octopus Home Mini keeps providing 30-second data for free
A Raspberry Pi 4 can run Postgres comfortably

decisions.question: Should the Lantern dashboard use Grafana or a custom UI?
decisions.reasoning: Native Postgres support, time-range pickers, alerting and annotations for free; a custom UI can come later if the dashboard outgrows it.

questions.text: How to downsample two years of 30-second data for graphs without losing the peaks?
